To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rate of selfing, population density, and the mode of pollen dispersals determine the genetic relationship within a seed population, and that the influence of dimensionality and range of pollen dispersal on genetic relationship is small.

(i) the coefficient of kinships between seeds, produced from different mother plants, is independent of the mode of pollen dispersaion, (ii) the rate of selfing and population density are important parameters for the genetic relationship among seeds, produced from one and the same mother plant, and (iii) the influence of the rate of pollen dispersal and population density on the coefficient of kinshp between seeds produced from different mother plant is small.

the genetic relationship within an open-pollination population is mainly determined by two factors, namely the rate of selfing and the population density, and that the range of pollen dispersal and the dimensionality of the population have little influence on the genetic relationships between seeds produced from the same plant or from plants that are located close to each other.
